verse_1:
Mind precedes all things,
Mind is chief, mind-made are they.
With a pure mind,
Word and deed bring ease.
verse_2:
Avoid all evil,
Cultivate the good,
Purify the mind —
This is the Buddhas’ teaching.
verse_3:
Breathing in, I know I breathe in,
Breathing out, I know I breathe out.
Body and mind in one rhythm,
This moment is at peace.
verse_4:
Like a lotus risen from the water,
Untouched by the mud.
The wise live in the world
With a mind forever pure.

article_1_ex: You need no cushion or quiet hour. Three mindful breaths between two meetings are enough to let the mind pause.
article_2_ex: The opening chapter of the Dhammapada puts the mind first. Read slowly, each verse speaks to life today.
article_3_ex: If a full day is hard, start with breakfast. What matters is compassion at every meal.
article_4_ex: Filial piety is not only for departed ancestors. Living parents are the nearest field of merit.
article_5_ex: Suffering, its cause, its end and the path are not abstract. One traffic jam shows all four truths.
article_6_ex: When sitting is hard, stand and walk. Walking meditation brings body and mind together.
article_7_ex: Those closest to us often hear our harshest words. Kind speech begins with a pause before speaking.
article_8_ex: Karma is not fate. To understand it is to see that every moment lets us plant a new cause.

help_meta_description: Frequently asked questions about your account, the lunar calendar, memorial book, practice and supporting InnerLamp.
help_search_placeholder: Search questions, e.g. memorial book, password
help_cta_text: Send your question to the InnerLamp team. We reply within one working day.
help_q_1: What if I forgot my password?
help_a_1: On the Log in screen choose “Forgot password” and enter the phone number you registered with. InnerLamp sends a verification code by text message so you can set a new password.
help_q_2: Can I use InnerLamp without an account?
help_a_2: Yes. The lunar calendar, sutras, bell and wooden fish, Buddha recitation and meditation work right away. You need an account to keep a practice journal, a memorial book, a family tree and to join a sangha.
help_q_3: How do I change my sangha?
help_a_3: Go to Me › Edit profile, pick “Your sangha” again and press Save changes.
help_q_4: Which time zone does the lunar calendar use?
help_a_4: Vietnam time (GMT+7), like the common almanacs in Vietnam. Auspicious days, auspicious hours and travel directions are for reference only.
help_q_5: What if a memorial date is the 30th and that lunar month has only 29 days?
help_a_5: The memorial book reminds you on the 29th of that month, as many families do.
help_q_6: My family lives abroad. Will memorial reminders land on the right day?
help_a_6: The lunar date is calculated in Vietnam time, then the reminder is shown in your phone’s local time. You can ask to be reminded 1, 3 or 7 days ahead in the memorial book.
help_q_7: How is the practice streak counted?
help_a_7: Each day you complete at least one session (meditation, Buddha recitation or sutra chanting) counts as a day. If you miss a day, the streak starts over.
help_q_8: Can I use the bell and wooden fish offline?
help_a_8: Yes. The bell and wooden fish, bead counting and the meditation timer all work offline.
help_a_9: No. InnerLamp is free for life: every feature is open to everyone, with no ads and no paid plan.
help_q_10: Will supporting InnerLamp charge me regularly?
help_a_10: No. Each contribution is recorded once for the amount you choose, with no monthly charge and no auto-renewal. To give again, you send a new one yourself.

legal_terms_intro: By using InnerLamp on the web and mobile app you agree to the terms below. Please read them carefully before creating an account.
legal_terms_s1_p1: Accessing or using InnerLamp means you agree to follow these terms. If you do not agree, please stop using the service.
legal_terms_s2_p1: You are responsible for keeping your password safe and for everything that happens in your account.
legal_terms_s2_p2: Each person should use one account. Profile information must be truthful and must not impersonate others or members of the Sangha.
legal_terms_s3_p1: Sutras, Dharma talks and guided meditations are provided for personal study and practice. You may not copy, republish or use them commercially without the consent of the author or rights holder.
legal_terms_s4_p1: InnerLamp is provided free for life. Contributions are voluntary, carry no special benefits and do not change the features available to you.
legal_terms_s4_p2: Each contribution is paid once, with no term, no automatic renewal and no recurring charge.
legal_terms_s5_p1: Shares and replies should be kind and respectful. InnerLamp may hide or remove content that is offensive, promotional, superstitious or exploitative.
legal_terms_s6_p1: Day selection, auspicious hours, travel directions and clashing ages are for reference only, following the traditional almanac. InnerLamp is not responsible for decisions made solely on this information.
legal_terms_s7_p1: We may update these terms as the service changes. Important changes will be announced in the app before they take effect.
legal_privacy_meta_description: How InnerLamp collects, uses and protects your data.
legal_privacy_intro: InnerLamp respects the privacy of your practice. This policy explains what data we collect, what we use it for and what rights you have.
legal_privacy_s1_p1: Account information: full name, dharma name, phone number, email.
legal_privacy_s1_p2: Practice data: sessions, streaks, bead counts, lamps lit.
legal_privacy_s1_p3: Family data you enter: memorial book, family tree.
legal_privacy_s2_p1: To run the features, send memorial and vegetarian-day reminders, sync data between web and phone, and improve the service. We do not sell your data.
legal_privacy_s3_p1: Your name, dharma name and photo are only shown to fellow members of your sangha when you turn on “Show my profile to members” in Settings.
legal_privacy_s3_p2: Your memorial book and family tree are visible only to you unless you choose to share them with relatives.
legal_privacy_s4_p1: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Only authorised staff can access it when needed to support you.
legal_privacy_s5_p1: You can view, edit, download or delete your data at any time in Settings › Account. When you delete your account, your data is permanently removed after 30 days.
legal_privacy_s6_p1: Anyone under 13 needs the consent and supervision of a parent or guardian to use InnerLamp.
temple_1_intro: A small temple in the heart of the city, home to the Tu Quang congregation of more than 180 lay Buddhists. It keeps a daily morning and evening chanting schedule, a monthly one-day retreat and a weekend Dharma class for teenagers.
temple_1_hl_1: One-day mindfulness retreat on the first Sunday of the month
temple_1_hl_2: Children’s Dharma class every Sunday morning
temple_2_address: Thanh Nien Street, Yen Phu, Tay Ho, Hanoi
temple_2_intro: Regarded as the oldest temple of Thang Long, founded in the Early Ly period on the Red River bank and later moved to a small peninsula on West Lake. Its eleven-storey Lotus Stupa is the temple’s best-known image.
temple_2_hl_2: Bodhi tree grafted from the tree at Bodh Gaya
temple_2_hl_3: Set on a peninsula in West Lake
temple_3_address: Ha Khe Hill, Kim Long, Hue
temple_3_intro: Built by Lord Nguyen Hoang in 1601 on Ha Khe Hill, on the left bank of the Perfume River. It was a royal temple under the Nguyen dynasty and is closely tied to the image of the old capital, Hue.
temple_4_address: Gia Sinh Commune, Gia Vien, Ninh Binh
temple_4_intro: A complex of the old Bai Dinh temple on the mountainside and a new temple area built from 2003. It is one of the north’s major pilgrimage centres, busiest during the spring festival season.
temple_4_hl_2: Phap Chu Hall housing a bronze Buddha statue
temple_4_hl_3: Spring festival from the 6th day of the first lunar month
temple_5_address: Chua Mot Cot Street, Ba Dinh, Hanoi
temple_5_intro: Built by King Ly Thai Tong in 1049 after a dream of Avalokitesvara seated on a lotus. The temple’s unique architecture resembles a lotus rising from Linh Chieu Pond.
temple_5_hl_1: A lotus pavilion on a single stone pillar
temple_5_hl_3: Next to the Ba Dinh historic area
temple_6_address: Huong Son Commune, My Duc, Hanoi
temple_6_intro: A complex of temples, shrines and caves in the Huong Son mountains, centred on Huong Tich Cave. Visitors take a boat along the Yen Stream; the pilgrimage season runs from the first to the third lunar month.
temple_6_hl_1: Huong Tich Cave — “first cave of the southern sky”
temple_6_hl_2: Boat ride on the Yen Stream
temple_6_hl_3: Festival from the 6th day of the first lunar month
temple_7_address: Bai But, Son Tra Peninsula, Da Nang
temple_7_intro: A temple on the Son Tra Peninsula overlooking Da Nang Bay. The 67-metre statue of Avalokitesvara faces the sea and is regarded by locals as a protector of fishermen.
temple_7_hl_3: Panoramic view of Da Nang Bay
temple_8_address: Phung Hoang Mountain, Tuyen Lam Lake, Da Lat
temple_8_intro: A large Zen monastery on Phung Hoang Mountain overlooking Tuyen Lam Lake. Practice follows the Truc Lam Yen Tu Zen lineage; the inner compound is reserved for resident monastics.
temple_8_hl_1: Tuyen Lam Lake at the foot of the mountain
temple_9_address: 339 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City
temple_9_intro: One of Saigon’s great temples, built in 1964 in northern Vietnamese style and named after the Vinh Nghiem ancestral temple in Bac Giang. It is known for its seven-storey Quan Am tower.
temple_9_hl_3: Lantern festival in the Vu Lan season
